record.context_brief: Binary scaling of hard electromagnetic probes
record.original_question: To what extent is the usual binary-scaling assumption valid for high-energy prompt-photon and high-invariant-mass dilepton production in nucleus-nucleus collisions, and how should deviations from binary scaling be separated into effects from nuclear parton distribution functions, proton-neutron parton-content differences, fragmentation photons, and any non-exactness of the scaling with the number of binary nucleon-nucleon collisions?

evidence.quote: These photons and dileptons provide an important bridge between proton-proton collisions and nucleus-nucleus collisions: their production in nucleus-nucleus collisions is simply an incoherent superposition of nucleon-nucleon collisions
The scaling of Eq. 5 with the number of binary nucleon-nucleon collisions N_binary is assumed to be exact.

Setting aside fragmentation photons, if Eq. 3 deviates from 1, it is understood to be due to the different parton content of nuclei compared to protons (a combination of nuclear parton distribution function and the different parton content of protons and neutrons).
Note that the idea that binary scaling is not exact has been explored in the literature (see Ref. [18] and references therein).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider high-energy nucleus–nucleus (A+A) collisions at collider energies, and the production of (i) high transverse-momentum prompt photons and (ii) high-invariant-mass Drell–Yan-type dileptons. The standard "binary collision scaling" hypothesis asserts that the inclusive cross section in A+A factorizes as

  dσ^{AA}/dX = N_bin · dσ^{NN}/dX,

where N_bin is the average number of inelastic binary nucleon–nucleon collisions in a given centrality class (computed from a Glauber model) and dσ^{NN}/dX is the inclusive elementary nucleon–nucleon cross section for the same observable X (e.g., photon p_T spectrum or dilepton invariant-mass spectrum). Equivalently, the nuclear modification factor R_AA(X) := (dσ^{AA}/dX)/(N_bin · dσ^{NN}/dX) is expected to equal 1.

Investigate the following question precisely:

(a) Under what kinematic regime (in p_T for prompt photons, and in invariant mass M and rapidity y for dileptons) and to what quantitative accuracy does the binary-scaling identity R_AA = 1 hold in QCD?

(b) Decompose any deviation R_AA(X) − 1 into the following four contributions and quantify each:
   (1) nuclear modifications of parton distribution functions (shadowing, anti-shadowing, EMC effect, Fermi motion), encoded in nPDFs f_i^{A}(x,Q^2) versus f_i^{p}(x,Q^2);
   (2) the isospin effect arising from the differing parton content of protons and neutrons (i.e., A consisting of Z protons and A−Z neutrons rather than A protons);
   (3) contributions of fragmentation photons (photons produced from the collinear fragmentation of a hard parton), which are sensitive to in-medium parton energy loss and therefore not expected to scale with N_bin;
   (4) any genuinely non-factorizing dynamical mechanism that makes the incoherent-superposition assumption inexact even after (1)–(3) are accounted for (e.g., coherent multi-nucleon scattering, initial-state energy loss, gluon saturation, Coulomb corrections, etc.).

Provide either rigorous bounds or controlled phenomenological estimates for each component, and determine whether, after subtracting (1)–(3), there is a residual deviation that signals a violation of exact binary scaling for these hard electromagnetic probes.
artifact.status_search_result: The validity of exact binary scaling for hard electromagnetic probes remains an active research topic. Experimental and theoretical studies (e.g., in nPDF global analyses, EPPS/nCTEQ frameworks, and direct-photon R_AA measurements at RHIC and the LHC) show that nuclear PDF modifications and isospin effects account for most observed deviations at high p_T, while fragmentation photons and possible coherent/energy-loss effects introduce additional, not yet fully disentangled, contributions. There is no consensus that the four contributions have been cleanly separated or that binary scaling is exact beyond nPDF/isospin corrections; the question is generally treated as open in the heavy-ion community.

status_evidence.title: Direct Photon Production in Heavy-Ion Collisions: Theory and Experiment
status_evidence.snippet: By comparing direct photon production in pp, p–A and A–A collisions, one can check the scaling with the number of binary collisions expected at a high transverse momentum range.
status_evidence.claim: Binary-scaling checks for direct photons are still being performed and remain an empirical/theoretical question.

status_evidence.title: PDFs, Shadowing and pA Collisions (CERN Yellow Report)
status_evidence.snippet: It is especially important to verify at what scale the observed nuclear dependence becomes universal and is completely determined by that of the nPDFs.
status_evidence.claim: Separating nPDF effects from other deviations of binary scaling is an ongoing research goal.

status_evidence.title: Coulomb corrections to photon and dilepton production in high-energy collisions
status_evidence.snippet: Coulomb corrections modify photon and dilepton production in nuclear collisions.
status_evidence.claim: Non-nPDF, non-isospin corrections to binary scaling exist and continue to be investigated.
